title: AI Food and Drink Videos With a Fresh Pour | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one bottle or can photo into a pour video with ice and fizz. Use a tall 9:16 size for TikTok and Reels, in clips of 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds.
h1: AI Food and Drink Videos From a Bottle Photo
lead: A shopper trusts the drink faster when the can and the pour share one shot. Pick a pour from the wall and use the package photo already on the listing.
steps_h2: How to Make a Beverage Video in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: The can and the glass stay in one shot, so shoppers see the drink they take home.

steps.d: Use the photo showing the full can, cap included, and pale soda color. Your chosen pour scene surrounds that can.
Yuzu, lightly sweet, over ice. That plain line is the script a voice can read.
A 9:16 pour fills a Story. A 1:1 of the can beside the glass fits the product page.

faq.q: What is a food and drink ad template?
faq.a: A food and drink ad template is a ready-made pour, glass, or sip built from your package photo. Shoppers recognize the package they will receive, and it stays readable when the sip happens.

faq.q: How does a drink template become a video?
faq.a: Use the listing photo, set the flavor line, and export a tall file for a Story. The package stays recognizable at the end of the pour.

faq.q: Why use this instead of filming a pour with a creator?
faq.a: You skip the search for a kitchen and a free afternoon that matches yours. The package photo is already on the listing, so the flavor can be advertised when it is ready to ship.

faq.q: Who is a drink template for?
faq.a: It is for drink brands that have to show the liquid, not only the label. A small founder can make the ad between production runs.

faq.q: Can a first-timer make a pour ad?
faq.a: Yes. A first pour does not require years in an editing job. Pick the glass scene. The package photo you already have is what the pour is built on.
Soda cans, cold brew bottles, and juice cartons fit when the package photo is clear. A loose splash with no package is a poor start.

faq.q: Can I use my can photo, a clip, and a logo?
faq.a: Yes. The package photo on your listing is the right file, logo and all. A clip of the tab opening can be the motion if you filmed one.

faq.q: Which placements and sizes fit a pour ad?
faq.a: A Story, the product page, YouTube, and a banner each have a size. A Story wants 9:16, usually at 6 or 10 seconds, so the pour stays full screen. The product page can use 1:1. YouTube can take 16:9, and 4:3 or 3:4 covers a banner. 15 and 30 seconds are there for a slower sip.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan to use a template?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. A photo spends 24 credits. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clip spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. The total shows before the run, and a failed run gives those credits back.

faq.q: Can I use the pour in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. Run the pour as an ad, and a client brand can put the same file on their product page. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: What does the pour template already include?
faq.a: The glass, the timing of the fizz, and where the package sits are already chosen. You write the flavor line. Label words can still be edited in a caption.

steps.prompt: A hand pours citrus soda from the silver can into one glass filled with ice. The shot starts at counter height and moves closer as the glass fills. Bright window light stays beside the can. The can and the full glass are both in the last shot. You hear a crisp fizz and a soft pour. Add background music if you want it. Keep the can's shape, color, and label as in your photo.

definition.title: What Is a Food and Drink Ad Template?
paras: A food and drink template is a finished scene for one moment, the pour or the first sip, built around the package you sell. The can or bottle stays in the frame on purpose.
The pour is ready to post once the package photo is in. One sip is the whole ad, and the package they take home stays readable.

reasons.h2: Why Sellers Start From a Template
reasons.lead: A flavor that showed up on Thursday can go out in an ad without a kitchen booking. A pour scene that already exists is how a drink shop moves.

items.d: The scene runs from the package photo you already have, so the ad does not wait on a kitchen booking or a person on camera.

items.t: Credits Instead of a Shoot Fee
items.d: New cuts spend credits on Starter at $24.50 a month, Pro at $35, or Premium at $63. What you do not pay a crew can stay on reaching buyers.

items.t: More Than One Cut to Test
items.d: Render a second hook and a second language from the same bottle photo. Keep the cut you want to spend on, and drop the one you do not.
Change the flavor name or the offer in the script and render again. Fixing a word does not mean calling a creator back.

items.t: No Hold on a Creator Calendar
items.d: The pour scene is available when the flavor is ready, including one you added late in the week. You are not holding a date on a creator's calendar.
You spend the words on the flavor and the ice, because the shot is already a can beside a filling glass. The camera move is already in the scene.

more_sections.lead: Voice, words on screen, music, and publishing sit with the glass scene, so the drink ad is finished here.

items.d: A stock voice, or a clone from a short sample, can name the flavor out loud.
The flavor and the sip can sit on screen, and you can slide that line in the editor before you export.
The same glass can serve each bottle you sell, so a flavor line gets more than one ad.
The pour can start from the bottle photo already on the product page. Paste that link and the scene uses the package there.
The AI video agent can draft a line about the pour, and you can change any word in it.

items.t: An AI Avatar Holds the Glass
items.d: An AI avatar can hold the glass or take the sip, so you do not book a creator for the pour. Add B-roll of the bottle alone when the label should fill the frame.
A track from the music library can sit under the pour, or the drink can be the only sound in the clip.
You can end the clip while the fizz is still visible and the flavor name is readable. The caption can sit beside the label.
The same pour can run in another language you sell in, with the spoken line and the captions switched.
Send the file to TikTok, or to Facebook and Instagram, from the account you connect. You can also download it and post on your own.

items.t: An API for the Whole Line
items.d: Your shop software can send bottle photos through the API when a flavor line needs many pours.
